description: Imposter — Mocking library with the perfect balance of Performance and Intuitive API
releaseNotes:
Performance

Unchanged imposters are reused across incremental runs (#178, closes #115; groundwork in #152, #175, #176, #177). The generator now builds each imposter from value models instead of Roslyn symbols, so an edit that doesn't change a target reuses its imposter. For 20 small imposters, a rerun after an unrelated edit went from 103 ms and 39.6 MB to 5.3 ms and 0.64 MB.

Diagnostics

IMP007: two registered targets that would generate the same imposter type, such as same-named interfaces nested in different classes, now report IMP007 instead of over 200 compile errors (#164, closes #128).

IMP008: a class target with abstract members your project can't override (internal or private protected members of another assembly) now reports IMP008 instead of generating an imposter that can't compile (#173, closes #148).

IMP009: a target whose impersonated members use Span\<T>, ReadOnlySpan\<T> or another ref struct in their signature now reports IMP009, naming the member and the type, instead of generating code with compile errors. The limitation is documented on the Limitations page (#202, closes #132).

IMP003 now stops generation for projects older than C# 9, the help links of all diagnostics point to the new Diagnostics page, and the unreachable IMP001 was retired (#142, closes #114).

Fixes

.NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Framework projects (#166, closes #131). Generated imposters compile for projects targeting .NET Standard 2.0 and later and .NET Framework 4.7.2 and later.

Virtual calls during construction (#156, closes #126). A target constructor calling a virtual member threw NullReferenceException inside the imposter. Such calls now run the base implementation or return defaults (see Limitations).

Init-only properties (#155, closes #130). Properties with init accessors generated ordinary setters that didn't compile.

Concurrent first calls (#157, closes #117). Concurrent callers could miss a configured outcome or see sequenced outcomes out of order, for methods, property getters and indexer getters.

Generic class methods:

base methods whose type parameters appear only in the return type, or not at all, are called with explicit type arguments (#158, closes #123);

overrides restate only the constraints C# allows (#159, closes #125).

Restricted accessors (#162, closes #122). Properties and indexers with a protected or otherwise restricted accessor are overridden legally, and accessors the project can't override are left alone.

Colliding inherited indexers (#163, closes #127). Indexers from different interfaces with the same parameter types are implemented explicitly.

Event handler order (#165, closes #129). Raising an event calls handlers in the order a C# event does, also after a handler is removed and added again.

Parameter modifiers:

in indexer parameters with base implementations (#168, closes #140);

async events whose delegate has in parameters (#170, closes #169);

ref readonly parameters (#172, closes #167).

Nullable annotations (#174, closes #161). Generated helpers keep T?, string? and nullable constraint annotations, so Returns((string?)null) compiles with nullable warnings as errors.

Name collisions in generated code. A target member, parameter or type parameter whose name matched something the generator declares broke the imposter. These names are now chosen around the target's names:

the instance's imposter field and the imposter builder fields (#182, closes #181; #185, closes #183);

constructor parameters named invocationBehavior or imposter (#188, closes #184);

event delegate parameters named like the raise methods' locals (callback, handler, task, pendingTasks) or the event builder's members (#187, closes #186; #191, closes #189);

event delegate parameters named Handler, Item1, Rest and other names C# reserves for tuple elements (#199, closes #190);

method parameters named like the method imposter's members, such as \_callbacks or DefaultResultGenerator (#194, closes #192);

indexer parameters named like the indexer imposters' members (#196, closes #193), other or hash (#197, closes #195);

parameters named like the arguments classes or their members, such as Equals on an indexer or As on a generic method (#200, closes #198).

Internal

CI fails when the committed generated-file snapshots are out of date (#154, closes #153), and pull requests must be up to date with master before merging (#203, closes #160).

Code scanning ignores source-generator output, so it reports only checked-in code (#204, closes #171).

The property builder field is described by the builder type (#180, closes #179).
